results.corrected_title: SV proposes a regulation to halt new data centres, modelled on the 1999 shopping-centre halt
results.corrected_summary: SV, through Storting representative Lars Haltbrekken, proposes a regulation under the Planning and Building Act that would halt new data centre developments until national rules are in place. Only data centres with a societally critical function would be exempt. The model is the temporary shopping-centre halt introduced in 1999 under the Bondevik government. SV chose a regulation over a law change because it would be faster.
key_facts: Proposer: SV (Lars Haltbrekken)
Instrument: regulation (forskrift) under the Planning and Building Act, not a law change
Halt lasts until national rules limiting data centre expansion exist
Exemption only for data centres with a societally critical function
Model: 1999 shopping-centre halt (Bondevik government), which lasted five years
Consultation period: six weeks
Reported by NTB on 2026-11-02
results.issues: Only one source opened (digi.no, citing NTB).

results.corrected_summary: CEO Melanie Perkins told staff on 2026-11-04 that a restructuring affects 1,271 people, about 22% of the company. Some will lose their jobs, some will change roles and some will be asked to relocate. The note does not say how many will actually be laid off. Perkins said growth slowed for the first time in a decade and that new technology is transforming how people create. The article does not itself state that AI caused the cuts.
key_facts: 1,271 people affected, about 22% of staff; the number of actual job losses is not stated
Perkins said growth slowed for the first time in a decade
In August Canva cut its 2026 revenue growth forecast from 30% to 20%
Product, Growth and Platform teams merge into one Product Org, and management layers are cut
From January most hybrid staff are expected in the office 2-3 days a week
Leavers get at least six months' salary
results.issues: Only TNW opened. Headlines saying '1,271 jobs cut' overstate it. AI link is framing by outlets, not a stated cause.

results.corrected_title: OpenAI makes 'dots' generally available in ChatGPT Enterprise, Edu and Healthcare
results.corrected_summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT Enterprise/Edu release notes dated 2026-11-04 introduce personal dots, which can keep working on tasks between conversations. They are generally available to eligible Enterprise, Edu and Healthcare workspaces, with an admin preview until 2026-11-18. After that date they are available by default. Admins can control who uses them, and dots support data residency and are HIPAA-eligible in covered workspaces.

Admin preview until 2026-11-18, when dots become default-on

results.corrected_title: Anthropic: Claude helped solve the first 3D structure of a bacterial vault particle
results.corrected_summary: Anthropic published a bioRxiv preprint on 2026-11-04. It reports the first 3D structure of a prokaryotic vault, built from the bacteriophage protein L05 in 96 copies, versus 78 in mammalian vaults. Claude searched a database of about 15 billion predicted proteins for vault relatives, and 7 of 15 tested candidates formed vault-like particles. An optimized isolation method takes about 90 minutes instead of about 3 days. The work is a preprint and has not been peer reviewed.
key_facts: Published 2026-11-04 as a bioRxiv preprint, not peer reviewed
L05 vault: 96 copies of one protein, versus 78 in mammalian vaults; about 9.5 MDa
7 of 15 candidate proteins formed vault-like particles under electron microscopy
Claude searched about 15 billion predicted proteins
Isolation takes about 90 minutes versus about 3 days conventionally
A flawed Claude-written protocol cost the team two weeks
results.issues: Only Anthropic's own post opened; no independent coverage.
